pages.title: What Raises It
pages.text: Instability is born of three old sins: silence, contradiction, and greed. Sparse books, random vows, clashing commands, strange terrain, cruel weather, crowded biomes, and mighty landmarks all make an Age restless.

pages.title: What Lowers It
pages.text: A named thing is calmer than an unnamed one. Give the Age land, biomes, time, sun, moon, stars, and weather. A single biome is a lullaby. A familiar world-shape is another. Even danger behaves better when invited by name instead of arriving through accident.

pages.title: Effects
pages.text: Every Age keeps a hidden fever. When it rises, the first signs are weakness and ill luck. Then come lightning, blasts, and decay creeping like mold through reality. The rot may bloom black or white, for each Age chooses its own pallor.

pages.title: Control
pages.text: Those with steward's authority may speak $(thing)/mystcraft instability toggle$() while standing in an Age. This stills or wakes the symptoms, not the sickness. The fever remains beneath the skin.
